Parameter Estimates of the Fitted Models

Source: R/parameter_table.R
parameter_table.Rd

Reports the maximum likelihood estimates of the parameters of each fitted model with their standard errors and Wald confidence intervals, on the natural scale of the distribution and/or on the transformed (real-line) scale on which flexsurv estimates them.

Usage

parameter_table(x, scale = c("natural", "transformed"))

Arguments

x

Object returned by fit_survival_models.

scale

Character vector with "natural" and/or "transformed". The default is both.

Value

A data frame with the columns fit_type, arm, model, parameter (name used by flexsurv, for example "shape", "gamma1" or "ARMTreatment"), scale, est, lcl, ucl and se, with one row per parameter and scale of each fitted model (models that failed are left out).

Details

On the transformed scale, the positive parameters (for example the shape and scale of the Weibull, see fit_survival_models) are on the log scale and the others, the arm effects and all spline parameters are untransformed; the confidence interval is est +/- z * se with z the normal quantile of the confidence level of the fit. On the natural scale, the estimate and the confidence limits of a log-transformed parameter are the exponentials of those on the transformed scale (as in flexsurvreg()$res) and the standard error is obtained by the delta method (est * se of the log). Arm effects in dependent fits are effects on the transformed location parameter (for example the log of the scale of the Weibull) on both scales. The shape of the Rayleigh model, fixed at 2, is not reported.

Examples

dat <- processing_dataset(
  system.file("extdata", "fit_example.csv", package = "SurvFitSummary"),
  column_arm = "TRT01P", column_survtime = "AVAL", column_cnsr = "CNSR",
  control_arm = "Control"
)
fits <- fit_survival_models(dat, distributions = c("exp", "weibull"),
                            spline_scales = NULL)
parameter_table(fits)
